scope: Proposition 4.1 (A process with verifiable transition probabilities) of the manuscript “Exact quantum factoring over a fixed finite gate set” (preprints/Exact-quantum-factoring-over-a-fixed-finite-gate-set-September-25-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 279 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 35e89279253b6c8a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a uniformly polynomial-time process, using the order trial of Proposition 3.1, with the following properties. 1. It either aborts or generates D. A deterministic polynomial-time verifier accepts exactly these complete data. The process’s classical controller makes at most L transitions, and completed runs are padded to exactly L by constant-output dummy transitions. Each transition output has a fixed W-bit encoding. 2. Given D and the recorded classical input of a transition, one can compute a good-output predicate, one canonical good encoding, and the exact probability s that an ordinary execution of that transition has a good output. The probability s is dyadic, has polynomial bit length, and obeys s ≥ 1 − 2−2n . For a dummy transition, its constant output is good and canonical, and s = 1. 3. Every evolution whose transition outputs are all good completes the tasks and generates D without aborting or reaching a resource cap. This assertion also holds when good outputs are supplied directly. The work is polynomially bounded on arbitrary output sequences as well, with malformed outputs causing an abort. Only the transition output is included in its W-bit encoding. Internal order-trial registers and recorded computational history are separate workspace and may be retained.
